problem: End-to-end ALFRED agents generalize poorly to unseen scenes, and prior hierarchical/SLAM methods (HLSM) use random exploration and lack fine-grained affordance-aware navigation. Navigating near an object is not enough; the agent must also end at a pose from which interaction is feasible.
motivation: With ground-truth navigation the framework reaches 64.6% SR on valid unseen, versus 11.8% for HLSM. Navigation that is affordance-aware is therefore the major bottleneck. Perturbing the target pose (random horizon or displacement) collapses performance, and exploration during inference counts toward the 1000-step budget, so exploration must be both efficient and task-driven.
key_idea: Build a waypoint-based affordance-aware semantic map (agent poses from which objects can be interacted with) through language-guided multimodal exploration, then plan over it with Dijkstra and hand off to an object-interaction transformer.
insight: Navigation pose precision is the bottleneck: the GT-navigation study shows SR falling from 64.6 to 21.7 with a random horizon and to 47.3 with random displacement. Ablations show every component matters: removing language from exploration drops SR from 17.68 to 4.30, random exploration gives 9.73, and removing the explored-area modality gives 15.17. Handling small and large objects differently is also important: instance-mask-only waypoints give 8.90 and map-only waypoints give 12.10.
method: Affordance-aware semantic map: a CNN predicts partial 37x37 (0.25 m cell) multi-hot maps of large-object classes and navigable area from images at 3 horizons. Partial maps are aggregated by Spatial Transformer with max-pooling, using known egomotion.

Waypoint generation for large objects: take the most confident map position for the class, snap it to the nearest navigable cell, choose the rotation that centers the object in view, and back up 1-3 steps by rule (3 for fridge) to leave room for articulated objects.

Waypoints for small objects: search all exploration frames for the Mask RCNN mask (confidence >= tau) with the largest area and use that pose. Fall back to the container's waypoint if no valid observation exists.

Multimodal exploration transformer: a cross-modal transformer over the current and next-subgoal language instructions, egocentric images and past actions, plus a CNN over a geometric explored-area map, feeds an MLP that predicts MoveAhead/RotateLeft/RotateRight/Stop. It is trained by imitation, with injected RotateRight and zigzag LookUp/LookDown actions for 360-degree, 3-horizon views.
Subgoal parser and target-object parser: Transformers on the language instruction classify a subgoal as navigation or not and predict the target object and its container.

Online planner: Dijkstra over the map to the waypoint, then a search over 6 horizons picking the one with the largest Mask RCNN mask (confidence > 0.8), with backtracking over h*, h*+15 and h*-15 if the following interaction fails.
Object interaction transformer: a subgoal-level cross-modal transformer trained by imitation that predicts actions plus masks for interaction subgoals.

setting.backbone: Custom transformers (exploration, parsers, object interaction) plus a CNN map predictor on ResNet-50 Faster RCNN features, with a pretrained Mask RCNN from E.T.; all trained on ALFRED
setting.training_data: ALFRED training split (21,023 tasks, 108 scenes) only. Map ground truth is generated from AI2-THOR APIs after manually fixing scene mismatches across THOR versions.
setting.observation: egocentric front-view RGB only (no depth or metadata at test time); agent knows its relative pose changes from discrete actions
setting.action_space: discrete: MoveAhead 0.25 m, RotateLeft/Right 90°, LookUp/Down 15°, plus 7 interaction actions with predicted masks

numbers_note: ALFRED is not in the canonical benchmark list, so it is labelled 'ALFRED' as in the list. Goal Condition is given as key GC.
results: AMSLAM reaches 23.48% SR / 34.64% GC on ALFRED test unseen and 17.68% / 33.96% on valid unseen. It beats the strongest baseline, HLSM (16.29 / 27.24 test unseen), and is described as a >40% relative improvement. Ablations show large drops for random exploration, no language, and the waypoint variants.
limitations: No instance-level representation, so multiple instances of the same object type are handled poorly
Only 108 training scenes leads to overfitting risk; demonstrated only on ALFRED with discrete actions and noise-free poses, not in noisy or real settings
Exploration steps consume the 1000-step budget, and zigzag and 360-degree injection triple the exploration cost
